desc: Ideation: reduce to `answer_i = max{d : d | A_i, cnt[d] ≥ K}`; design hybrid small-`d`/block sieve; prove intra-block non-collision and slice-length invariants
Write the complete solution script (I/O parse, phase 1 `cnt`, phase 2 `f`, output) with parameter `S` and clamped block bounds
Verify `np.copyto(f[k*lo:k*hi+1:k], vals, where=mask)` behaves as intended (basic slicing yields a writable view; masked in-place write is valid)

Correctness check: sample 1 traced by hand (3/4/6/1/6); edge cases verified logically (`M+1 < S` ⇒ `tmax=0` and small-`d` loop covers all `d`; `M=1`; `K=1` gives `f[v]=v`; `K=N`; `d=1` base case via `f=ones`)
Performance review: ~1.4·10⁷ element touches per phase, ~15 000 NumPy calls, int32 arrays, vectorized uint8 parser, block skipping when no good `d`; peak memory ~60 MB during parse
Final assembly: single clean script, no debug output
